evals.name: correct-but-terse-is-left-alone
evals.setup: `Get`'s godoc is a single accurate sentence that already states the one thing the signature cannot — that a miss returns the zero value rather than an error.

evals.name: adds-only-confirmable-facts
evals.setup: `Store` mutates the slice it is passed — the body proves it. It has no mutex and no synchronization of any kind, so whether it is safe for concurrent use is simply open: the code neither establishes nor rules it out. Its godoc states neither fact.

evals.name: directives-and-interface-method-godoc
evals.setup: `./pkg/io` carries a `//go:build` line, a `//go:generate` directive, and a `Read` method implementing `io.Reader` whose godoc restates the interface contract and nothing more.

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: An ordinary single-function run that changes one godoc and deletes one inline comment.

evals.name: line-target-resolves-to-its-item
evals.setup: Line 42 of `pkg/svc/foo.go` is inside the body of `(*Svc).Flush`, where `// increment i` sits above `i++`. The file holds four other functions.

evals.name: module-mode-with-fanout-and-filter
evals.setup: A module of eleven packages, two of them `svc` and `api`. `api` holds a `Router` — a map-backed struct with no mutex and no synchronization of any kind, whose godoc says nothing about concurrency. Whether it is safe for concurrent use is simply open: the code neither establishes nor rules it out.

evals.name: side-effect-is-not-a-surprise
evals.setup: Two `io.Writer` implementations, both pinned by `var _ io.Writer = (*T)(nil)` and both carrying godoc. `(*fileSink).Write` writes the bytes to a file and nothing else — the job the method exists to do, side effects and all. `(*teeSink).Write` also writes a copy to a second sink the interface knows nothing about, and returns `len(p)` even when that second write fails.
